lesson_title: One Wallet, One Street, One Cooler Box: Half a Year of Economics
hook_text: R400 in the wallet. R600 on the list. That gap is an entire school subject.
clip_script: Month-end. The wallet holds four hundred rand and the list holds six hundred rands' worth of needs. That gap is the whole subject of economics — not a bad month, a permanent condition. And every choice has a price tag behind the price tag: buy the school shoes, and the real cost is the best thing those rands would otherwise have done. Now follow the money. Friday afternoon, one street: the factory pays wages, workers spend at the spaza and the salon, the takings pay more wages — money moving in a circle, with three drains emptying it and three taps refilling it. And at the taxi rank, a cooler box of cold drinks settles the oldest argument in the world: thirty rand and they sit sweating in a pile; five rand and the queue clears them by noon; somewhere between, the pile and the queue both vanish — and nobody needed a committee. Scarcity, the circular flow, equilibrium: half the year, three objects. The exam is asking about your own street.
visual_style: A wallet opening beside a growing shopping list; coins flowing in a glowing circle around a street of small shops with taps and drains; a cooler box with a price tag flipping between numbers as a pile shrinks and a queue forms.
mood: Warm, grounded, quietly revelatory — everyday objects turning into exam structures.
pacing: Steady open on the wallet, flowing middle around the street, snappy beats at the cooler box, confident landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision sweep and take the whole half-year into the exam as three structures.
